clue.text: Fruit put in piles in lines

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
to rick is to stack hay or corn into ricks, that is, piles

explanation.surface: Someone stacks fruit in heaps arranged in neat rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like part of the stacking picture, but it is the definition: a whole verse form described as so many lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-line comic poem is a set of verse lines, so the poem can be called simply lines.

clue.text: Irritable in uniform

explanation.surface: A grumpy person wearing a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is an old word for liverish, bad-tempered; it also means the distinctive dress of servants or a company.

clue.text: State conceals one murder, the result of using a chopper

definitions.text: the result of using a chopper

indicators.note: conceals means holding something inside, so the state wraps the other pieces

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine
an ace is a one in cards
to do in is to murder

explanation.surface: A state covers up a killing carried out with an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests an axe murder, but it is a kitchen knife chopping vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A macedoine is a mixture of diced fruit or vegetables, what a cook's cutting produces.

clue.text: A sort of miracle, what the Dutch do to polders

definitions.text: what the Dutch do to polders

indicators.note: sort of suggests a version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Draining the Dutch lowlands is a kind of miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: Polders are low-lying lands won back from the sea in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch win back land from the sea by draining it, so they recover it for use.

clue.text: Anger which a fellow suppresses

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down inside, so the letters are tucked within these words

explanation.surface: A man holds back his rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to feel irritated or annoyed, a mild form of anger.

clue.text: Waterproof stuff — it's about to be incorporated in a raincoat

indicators.note: to be incorporated in signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters of it's are read backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A note on a waterproofing compound being worked into a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the it's letters, and 'to be incorporated in' sets that run inside the coat; 'a' before raincoat is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin-based paste used as a sealant to keep water out.

clue.text: Still by no means 'irsute

indicators.note: the apostrophe in place of H shows the H is dropped, Cockney style

parts.note: by no means hairy, the meaning of hirsute, is bald, without hair

explanation.surface: Someone still not at all 'airy, in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by no means hirsute' gives HAIRLESS; the apostrophe where the H of 'irsute' should be says drop the H, leaving AIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Still air is calm with no breeze, so a still day is without wind.

clue.text: Beginners, toying with a new guitar, pluck a string

indicators.note: beginners means the starting letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Novices fiddle with a new guitar and pluck a string.
explanation.definitionFit: To twang is to sound a taut string with a sharp vibrating note.

clue.text: Top of cedar in Knossos, perhaps — material .

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word in a down clue

parts.note: Knossos is a site on the island of Crete, so it is on Crete

explanation.surface: Cedar timber at the Minoan palace of Knossos is the building material.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 9-down's, but each answer stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete is a building substance made of cement, sand and gravel.

clue.text: . yielding couch for king in the east

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: the Orient is the east
R stands for rex, Latin for king
a bed is a couch

explanation.surface: A soft couch for an Eastern king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' seems to describe the couch, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone yielding gives way to others' wishes, compliant and dutiful.

clue.text: As a court official, I can have climber disciplined

indicators.note: disciplined suggests the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A royal courtier claims the right to punish a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disciplined' rearranges all fifteen letters of I CAN HAVE CLIMBER; 'As a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: This title belongs to a senior officer of the royal household, deputy to the Lord Chamberlain.

clue.text: Broadcast rebuke about help being turned back

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

indicators.note: being turned back says the letters of help's synonym are read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's scolding is overturned when assistance arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being turned back' reverses the help synonym, and 'about' has the scolding word wrap round it; 'rate' meaning scold is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to send out in all directions, as light or heat spreads from a source.

clue.text: Ship's doctor right about lip

indicators.note: about means going round, so the doctor-and-right pair wraps the lip

parts.note: a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: The ship's medic is correct about someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's doctor' reads as one person, but 'Ship' alone is the definition; 'about' has the doctor-and-right pair go round the lip word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel that scoops mud and silt from a harbour or channel bed.

clue.text: Bespangled girl rejected advance payment

indicators.note: rejected suggests something thrown back, so the girl's word is read backwards

parts.note: maid is an old word for a girl
an ante is a stake put up in advance, as in poker

explanation.surface: A glittering young woman turns down a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MAID into DIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamanté describes fabric decorated with glittering sequins or paste jewels, i.e. spangled.

clue.text: Mark's boat in difficulties in river

indicators.note: in places the scrambled boat inside the river

parts.note: the Nene is a river in eastern England

indicators.note: in difficulties suggests trouble, the boat's letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man named Mark has his boat in trouble on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is a note mark in text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag, written NB, is a marker telling a reader to note well.

clue.text: Ecstatic about money that's disbursed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: sent is slang for carried away, enraptured
P stands for penny or pence, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about cash that has already been paid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Money disbursed has been paid out, used up.

clue.text: Sally escorted by people in extra-terrestrial gear

indicators.note: in places sally-and-people inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the alien of the film, short for extra-terrestrial
a sally is a witty remark, a quip
men means people

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally goes out with people wearing space suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a witty remark; 'escorted by' puts the people after it, and 'in' sets both inside the film alien's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is the kit, tools and apparatus needed for a job.

clue.text: Boss the fellow with authority in this rural business

parts.note: a boss is a knob or stud
arm means power, as in the arm of the law

explanation.surface: The boss, the man in charge of a country enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the raised knob on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm where horses are bred is a kind of agricultural enterprise.

clue.text: While speaking, adjusts clothing

indicators.note: while speaking signals the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to true something is to adjust it until it is accurate, as with a wheel

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks their outfit while giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are tartan trousers, a garment and so a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Drain from sink

explanation.surface: Water drains from a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scupper is a hole letting water off a ship's deck; to scupper is to sink a ship deliberately.

clue.text: Working hard in recession, extracting from niobium the core metal

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: at it is an idiom for busy, working hard

indicators.note: extracting means taking letters out of the word niobium
the core says the letters removed come from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A busy metallurgist in a slump digs out the heart of an element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns AT IT into TITA; 'extracting' and 'the core' remove OBI from the middle of NIOBIUM, leaving NIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light, silvery element, one of the metals.

clue.text: Capital chap included in North American XI

indicators.note: included in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: XI is eleven, written 11 and read as the Roman numeral II
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man selected for a North American eleven, a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: XI looks like a team of eleven players but gives 11, read as II.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the chief city of Kenya, its seat of government.

clue.text: Family tree

explanation.surface: A family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty; the citrus fruit grows on the tree of the same name.

clue.text: Interrupt routines in attempt to make a comeback

indicators.note: to make a comeback means to return, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in places routines inside attempt

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
ruts are dull fixed routines

explanation.surface: Breaking into someone's habits while trying a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the routines inside the attempt, giving BRUTSID, which 'to make a comeback' reads backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to break in on them, to interrupt.

clue.text: Jack used to catch mackerel

explanation.surface: A man named Jack goes mackerel fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is a nursery-rhyme figure; 'a sprat to catch a mackerel' is a proverb for a small outlay to win a big prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme Jack who ate no fat bore that surname; and a small fish of that kind is bait for bigger ones.

clue.text: A mule, perhaps — one unsteady on his feet

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal that keeps stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless shoe, an example of a slipper; and someone who slips is unsteady on their feet.

clue.text: Gentleman of dissolute habits, no end of an upstart

indicators.note: dissolute suggests loose living, so the letters of habits are loosened and rearranged
no says the letter taken from upstart is subtracted from the rearranged letters
end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gentleman of loose habits, unlike some upstart.
explanation.walkthrough: HABITS rearranged, less T (the last letter of 'upstart'), gives the answer; 'dissolute' signals the rearrangement and 'no' the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful Indian form of address for a European man of standing.

clue.text: An editor can hope for circulation that's a little of what's required

indicators.note: for circulation suggests the letters are sent round and mixed up

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hopes for readership figures that meet the need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for circulation' looks like newspaper sales but rearranges AN EDITOR CAN HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a tiny amount, insignificant against what is needed.

clue.text: In defeat, you are said to grow up

indicators.note: In places the spoken letters inside defeat's synonym

parts.note: to mate in chess is to defeat the king

indicators.note: said signals letters chosen for how they sound

parts.note: said aloud, you sounds like the letter U; said aloud, are sounds like the letter R

explanation.surface: Someone in defeat is told they need to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns the two words into the letters they sound like, and 'In' sets them inside the chess word for defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to develop fully, to become adult.

clue.text: Sailor's in the drink

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman; with the 's it gives ABS

explanation.surface: A sailor has fallen into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' reads as the sea, but 'drink' alone defines; 'in' and 'the' are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit, a type of alcoholic drink.
